newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India stabilises, buying of second line.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India stabilises, buying of second line.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts saw some buying of second line stocks after Finance Minister P Chimbdambaram failed to lift markets with his budget statement.
"Foreign investors had not expected much from the budget speech, but the locals were looking for incentives," said a trader.

The James Capel Indian GDR Index rose 0.39 points, 0.56 percent to 70.24 points, a premium of 14.83 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 44.17 points, 1.3 percent, to 3,347.7.
"There was some buying of second line stocks, Sanghi Polyester, Garden Silks, Finolex and the like, but not much," said the trader.
He also notes that ITC and the hotel stocks had turned higher.
Indian Hotels added 38 cents to $25.65/$26.65, while East India Hotels put on to $20.25/$21.25, while ITC added 19 cents $8.50/$9.25.

"For most of the week traders in London have been watching how British football clubs got on in Europe," said the trader, who supports Arsenal, which lost its latest match against continental European opposition.

Elsewhere in Asia, the Capel Korea Index fell 0.04 points 0.07 percent to 67.11 points, a premium of 24.15 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index The composite stock index shed 12.38 points or 1.55 percent to provisionally close at 785.19.
The Capel Taiwan Index rose 1.47 points, 1.66 percent, to 90.55 points, a premium of 4.44 percent over the local market after Taiwan Weighted Indes rose 45.95 points or 0.72 percent to 6,471.63.
